context.framing: Discrete optimization with a moved goalpost. A PREVIOUS campaign took pscalib.calib from 560.9 to 37.4 ms/event using an OPTIONAL numba kernel and landed 5.4x end-to-end; that work is open as PR #17 on branch cand/calib-speedup at SHA 5c432ecd and MUST NOT be disturbed. This campaign forbids numba, so the remaining speed has to come from somewhere else. Objective: minimize total ms/event at workers=1. The 645.3 ms/event budget decomposes, all terms measured: psdata read 38.7 + stack 10.4 + pscalib.calib 560.9 + the harness's own isfinite/where/float64-accumulate 35.3. With the harness frozen the irreducible floor is 84.4 ms and the ceiling is 7.65x, so 8.0x is UNREACHABLE without also attacking the harness scaffolding — overlapping the read is what makes the target possible at all. Two move sets. In pscalib, numpy only: (a) relayout constants to (seg,row,col,gain) so a mixed-gain gather reads one cache line instead of touching three separate 201 MB planes; (b) take_along_axis in place of the remaining np.select lanes; (c) an out= parameter so the 67 MB output buffer is reused rather than first-touched every event; (d) fewer numpy passes per tile via in-place ops and out= everywhere. In the harness: (e) a stdlib-thread prefetch double-buffering read_events so the 38.7 ms read OVERLAPS compute instead of adding to it; (f) reuse the stack buffer; (g) fuse the isfinite/where pass with out=. Surrogate objectives, both statically countable: DRAM bytes moved per event, and numpy passes per tile. Known floors, measured: pure-G0 frames already run 18.5 ms at ~251 MB/event = 13.6 GB/s, i.e. AT the streaming roofline; the two-plane blend's DRAM floor is 368 MB/event = ~22 ms at 17 GB/s, and the measured pure-numpy blend is ~4x off that, the gap being L1/L2 traffic from ~7 numpy passes per tile rather than DRAM. So calib in pure numpy plausibly reaches 35-45 ms and cannot go below ~22. Each accepted move re-ranks the remaining ones; re-measure every iteration. Do NOT spend budget re-deriving what is already measured above, and do NOT re-try what the previous campaign already exhausted: tile size is flat (68-71 ms across 128-1024 rows), the no-op astype copies are already deleted, the sparse masked-pixel fixup is already in, and the constant-mask hoist — half the original cost — is already landed on cand/calib-speedup.

context.baseline: Measured, July, job 31397423 on sdfmilan053: jungfrau, exp=mfx100848724 run=51, 512 events at 33.5 MB/event, workers=1 evt_per_s=1.55 = 645.3 ms/event; workers=16 evt_per_s=10.58. Constants are (3,32,512,1024) float32 = 201 MB each for pedestals, pixel_gain, pixel_offset, plus (3,32,512,1024) uint64 = 402 MB pixel_status. No 'mask' constant is supplied. Real r51 data is 83.8% gain stage 0 and 16.2% stage 1, with stage 2 at 0.0011% and the bad code at 0.0000003%; the harness's own 512-event mix has mean non-G0 fraction 0.2027, median 0.1134, max 0.9949. The pure-numpy cost curve SATURATES and turns down above frac ~0.3 (at frac=1.0 every pixel reads a single plane), so the worst case is MIXED frames near 0.3, not the highest-frac frame, and a linear a+b*frac fit is pessimistic at the top end. workers=16 is currently I/O-bound and buys approximately nothing once calib is cheap: print it for the record, never threshold it.
context.instrument: The proof job runs THREE arms in ONE slurm job on ONE exclusive sdfmilan node at 512 events, so every denominator is measured now rather than quoted from July: arm before_orig = incumbent pscalib c5ce538 + the UNMODIFIED harness (must reproduce ~645 ms/event); arm after_orig = candidate pscalib + the UNMODIFIED harness (isolates pscalib's own contribution); arm after_fast = candidate pscalib + the PATCHED harness (the 8.0x claim). The threshold ratio is before_orig/after_fast at workers=1; print after_orig/before_orig and after_fast/after_orig alongside so the two contributions are separable. Each arm asserts its pscalib SHA, its src md5, and the md5 of the harness file it loaded. Four hard-won rules, all of which cost the previous campaign real budget: (1) 128 events is UNUSABLE as a metric — identical code gave 4.31x and 1.33x depending on arm order — so every quoted number comes from 512 events; (2) SERIALIZE your own jobs and verify node exclusivity before submitting — the previous campaign destroyed three runs with a self-inflicted I/O storm from its own concurrent xtc readers; (3) arm symmetry is checked by BYTES READ per arm, never by MB_per_s — MB_per_s is just nbytes/wall with nbytes fixed by the event count, so the old reject rule is a wall-time symmetry test in disguise that ANY real speedup above ~1.18x must fail; it made all three previous proof jobs exit rc=96 while every arm exited rc=0, and its firing carries ZERO contention information. Do not inherit that rule; if you keep it, treat rc=96 as uninformative and say so. (4) The harness's own GATE PASS / PURITY=PASS / partition_invariant lines do NOT test byte-exactness — run_gate never compares calib to a reference and PURITY=PASS only asserts isfinite(cal).any() — so the load-bearing evidence is the bit gate you run yourself inside the arm.
context.gate_design: Gate candidates against the FROZEN pure-numpy reference outputs in _cand/fixture/ (the verbatim c5ce538 output on real frames), not against psana, so the inner loop needs no psana environment; c5ce538 is already proven max|diff| == 0 versus det.raw.calib(evt), so equality with it transitively gives equality with psana. The gate is THREE CONJUNCTS and all three are load-bearing: identical NaN masks; uint32 bit equality on the non-NaN set; signbit equality wherever the value is zero. A plain max|diff| == 0 check is a PROVEN HOLE — writing masked pixels as literal +0.0 instead of -0.0 passes it while differing in 221-4456 bit patterns, because pixel_gain for stages 1 and 2 is entirely negative. Span the non-G0 range, not one frame: a float64-chain mutation fails 7 of 8 frames but PASSES the frac=0.0000 frame. Also carry forward the defect the previous campaign found the hard way: classifying the gain stage with `a >= 0x4000` is False for every negative word, so SIGNED raw with negative values silently kept its stage-0 value while the reference renders 0.0 — non-unsigned raw must defer to the verbatim reference, and a robustness check that casts a uint16 fixture slice upward CANNOT catch this. Run the full psana gate (pscalib's own test_calib_us000.py against det.raw.calib and det.raw.image) once, at the end, as the final proof. SEPARATELY, the patched harness must be numerically inert: the binned cube it produces must be BIT-IDENTICAL to the unmodified harness's cube over the same events, so that no speedup is bought by changing the accumulation dtype or the science.
context.numpy_only: Numpy alone, and this is a feasibility gate rather than a preference. No numba and no njit anywhere under src/ — not optional, not behind try/except, not in a comment-referenced code path. No OTHER new runtime dependency either: no numexpr, no cython, no compiled extension, no pythran. The stdlib is fine, and the harness prefetch is expected to use stdlib threading. Keep python-3.9 compatibility and numpy 1.26.4 semantics, because that is what the psana release ps_20241122 provides. Note that np.select over float32 choices with an integer default stays float32 in numpy 1.26.4, which is what makes the reference arithmetic pure single precision.

operating_mode.role: You are an orchestrator. Each iteration (= one turn): think about the next slice, decompose it, delegate, then integrate and ledger. Every decision is yours — advisors advise, they never decide and never execute. When you overrule an advisor, record the dissent in the ledger rather than deleting it. A worker's report is provenance 'inherited' until you re-verify the artifact yourself; re-verify anything a later iteration will stand on. Workers return evidence, not conclusions: artifacts and identifiers (job ids, SHAs, paths, raw printed output) plus an explicit list of what was NOT done or NOT checked. Prefer the Workflow tool over the Agent tool whenever Workflow is available. The user's approval of this contract authorizes the Workflow tool for delegation, including per-agent model and reasoning-effort overrides.
operating_mode.budget: Delegate to at least 2 and at most 5 subagents per iteration. Advisors convened in an iteration count toward that budget, so shrink the worker count to stay within it.
operating_mode.advisors: planner (opus, xhigh effort) — consulted BEFORE a decomposition is committed, at iteration 1 and at any iteration that changes direction or commits a large share of remaining budget. Mandate: attack the plan; is this the right question, decomposition, stopping rule? Run a pre-mortem naming the most likely way the iteration wastes its budget and the earliest observable sign it is happening. Adjudicate contested calls in writing, preserving the losing argument. skeptic (opus, xhigh effort) — consulted AFTER results, BEFORE belief, on every iteration that produces a measurement; always a fresh invocation, never the planner. Mandate: refute, not review. Per claim ask: too big or too small to be true? is there an independent cross-check (second instrument, conservation identity, repeat with one variable changed)? would the leading alternative mechanism have looked any different? do the books balance? could the check it passed have failed at all? Verdict per claim: BELIEVE, or QUARANTINE with the reason. cold-reader (xhigh effort) — once the deliverable claims to be usable and again after each round of fixes, given the deliverable and NOTHING else: attempt to use it end to end, log every stumble, repair nothing. Verdict: usable from the artifact alone, or not, with the blocking defect named.
operating_mode.discipline: Predict before you measure: write the expected value or band into the ledger BEFORE the measurement runs; a post-hoc band always agrees and proves nothing. Quarantine has teeth: a claim the skeptic rejects is not tagged verified and is not used as a premise later until new evidence resolves the objection. One writer per scarce resource — each candidate worktree, the slurm allocation, the git index, the harness file — serialize with explicit gates and never assume a queue means free. Advisors receive the evidence and the question, never the answer you hope for.
operating_mode.delegation_guard: Give every worker a cadence with a number in it, so silence is legible as failure and a kill loses little: work in batches of about 12 items, writing results for every id to the output file before starting the next batch, never reading the whole list before writing anything. Poll running agents about every 5 minutes on transcript BYTES, not wall-clock (wall-clock cannot distinguish slow from stuck): trip at 70 MB or at 3x the median sibling. On a trip, SendMessage the agent asking only how many items completed, how many written, which batch, and which item it is reading now. Circling looks like the same items re-read, nothing appended, a plan restated rather than advanced, or an answer naming no number — then TaskStop, keep what it wrote, and relaunch the remainder on a cheaper instrument with a batch cadence rather than the same instrument with a sterner prompt. An agent that has produced no artifact is not still working.
operating_mode.iterations: Complete at least 5 iterations before done_when may be considered met, even if it appears satisfied earlier — use surplus iterations to push the frontier further and to harden what is already measured.
operating_mode.ledger: Maintain .goal/pscalib-numpy-only-8x.ledger.json on disk, appending one FULL entry per iteration: {n, thought, prediction, delegated: [{agent, task, model, effort}], integrated, new, remaining} — the file keeps every field. 'prediction' records the expected value or band written BEFORE any measurement that iteration ran. 'new' must name a decision or artifact that did not exist before this iteration. At the end of EVERY turn print a LEDGER digest (NOT the whole file): a header line `LEDGER pscalib-numpy-only-8x — iterations N/5, full at .goal/pscalib-numpy-only-8x.ledger.json` (N = completed-iteration count); then one roster line per completed iteration `n · delegated:k · new: <that iteration's non-empty new>` (k = subagents delegated that iteration); then the current iteration's full JSON entry in a fenced block. operating_mode.claims: Maintain .goal/pscalib-numpy-only-8x.claims.json on disk — the campaign's key claims (typically 5-15), updated every iteration as claims land or change. Shape: {goal, slug, claims: [{id, provenance, evidence, claim}]} — goal and slug are set at bootstrap, keep them. provenance is one of: verified — evidence cites a checkable artifact you surfaced yourself in this conversation (slurm job id, git SHA, output you printed from your own run); inherited — the evidence you hold is a report rather than the artifact: an external source, or a subagent's account of its own work (name the agent and task).
